chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Ahmad ibn Idris - may God be pleased with him - narrated from his father, who said: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Imran al-Ash'ari narrated to me through a chain known to reach Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him).
He said: Wastefulness (saraf) is in three things: wearing out your decent garment, throwing date seeds to the right and left, and pouring away leftover water.
And he said: There is no wastefulness in eating.
ai.seo_question: What are the three acts considered wastefulness in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Khisal*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) identifies three specific acts of *saraf* (wasteful excess): degrading one's modesty through clothing, carelessly discarding date seeds, and pouring away surplus water. He notably clarifies that mere consumption of food does not constitute wastefulness, distinguishing between necessary use and excessive disposal. This teaching reflects the Shia emphasis on environmental stewardship and moderation in daily life, linking physical actions to spiritual integrity.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 3-37 Al-Hussein ibn Ahmad ibn Idris - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Imran al-Ash’ari linked it up through a chain of narrators to Aba Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB) who said, “Three things would constitute being wasteful: wearing indecent garments, throwing away a date seed, and pouring away your leftover water.”
The Imam (MGB) added, “There is no wastefulness in eating.”
